recorded_uses.name: Turmeric
recorded_uses.pros: Laboratory work shows curcuminoids inhibit platelet activation.
recorded_uses.cons: No clinical clot evidence, and curcumin is poorly absorbed on its own.
recorded_uses.cautions: Does not replace an anticoagulant; may add to bleeding risk and slow drug breakdown.
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of haridra as an anti-inflammatory herb that moves the blood.
recorded_uses.condition_name: Blood clot in a vein (DVT or pulmonary embolism)

recorded_uses.name: Turmeric
recorded_uses.pros: Kitchen spice; laboratory work supports anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet actions.
recorded_uses.cons: No outcome evidence in heart disease, and curcumin is poorly absorbed.
recorded_uses.cautions: May add to bleeding risk and slow the breakdown of some heart medicines.
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of haridra as an anti-inflammatory herb.
recorded_uses.condition_name: Prevention of a further heart attack or stroke

recorded_uses.name: Turmeric
recorded_uses.pros: Everyday kitchen spice; animal and early human work suggests better glucose control.
recorded_uses.cons: Curcumin is poorly absorbed alone; evidence is early; can irritate the stomach.
recorded_uses.cautions: May slow breakdown of other medicines; a documented interaction with metformin exists.
recorded_uses.source_note: PMID 29518605 (curator-confirmed metformin interaction in this project); antiplatelet tag from PMID 16112857 and PMID 20158382
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of haridra for prameha, inflammation and skin disorders.
